title: Workplace psychological safety indicators and MOM's approach
asked: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan asked whether the Ministry of Manpower has considered developing workplace psychological safety indicators or benchmarks to complement existing workplace well-being initiatives, and if not, whether it intends to do so.
response: MOM recognises psychological safety's role in a positive work environment, but says other factors like job demands, peer relationships and supervisor support also affect mental well-being. Its approach is to help employers assess and address mental well-being holistically rather than set national-level indicators or benchmarks for psychological safety alone. It points to iWorkHealth, an online psychosocial health assessment tool that gives employers an aggregated, anonymised report on work stressors and risks, including psychological safety, plus recommendations. The Tripartite Advisory on Mental Health and Well-being at Workplaces is cited as a complementary resource.
